events.title: Radical Inclusion
events.description:
The world can often feel divided and exclusionary. What would it mean to turn that on its head? This workshop explores how we can actively include ourselves and others, while acknowledging the real need for both inclusive and separatist spaces. 
Together, we will examine the barriers that create exclusion—such as access, power dynamics, and social norms—and explore practical ways to respond to them. The focus is on finding a balance between collective needs and individual experiences, and reimagining what truly supportive spaces can look like. 
Led by Caritia, this session offers a space for reflection, discussion, and collaborative thinking. Participants will be invited to design and imagine the kinds of groups and environments they would want to be part of, while developing tools to meaningfully include difference and diversity for the benefit of all. 
What we’ll cover


What “radical inclusion” means in practice 


The role of exclusion: boundaries, safety, and separatist spaces 


Identifying barriers to inclusion (access, identity, power) 


Balancing individual needs with group dynamics 


Designing spaces you would actually want to belong to 


Practical strategies for including difference and diversity

Lajos Meinberg grew up in a family of musicians, which nurtured his love for jazz from an early age. Since 2020, he has been studying at the Jazz Institute Berlin under Wolfgang Köhler, Tino Dorado, and Bastian Stein, and has been actively involved in the Berlin jazz scene since then. He has had the opportunity to perform with musicians such as Rodney Green, Doug Weiss, Matt Wilson and Martin Wind. Lajos received the Ingolf Burkhardt Award in 2022 and won first prize at the International Jazzhaus Piano Competition in Freiburg in 2024, as well as second prize at the International Jazz Piano Competition Lausanne in 2025. In August 2023, Lajos was part of the Elbphilharmonie Jazz Academy, where he had the chance to learn from musicians like Anat Cohen, Donny McCaslin, and Sullivan Fortner.
Johann Greve is a double bassist and composer from Lower Saxony. Since moving to Berlin in 2019, he has worked as a sideman on a wide variety of projects and established himself in the young Berlin jazz scene. He has performed with Percy Pursglove, Julius Gawlik, Charlotte Greve and Olga Reznichenko, among others. In March 2024, he recorded material for his debut album with his quartet.
California-born drummer Genius Wesley is an emerging force on the international jazz scene, known for his electrifying energy, deep musicality, and fearless improvisation. The band Hunger, consisting of Christoph Rothmeier and Jörg Hochapfel, has been around since 1996, initially on Lake Constance, then for a long time in Hamburg, and finally in Berlin.
Previously known in the music world for their ""abstract pop studies with a Dadaist bent"" (taz) and ""nervous disco-punk racket"" (Tagesspiegel), they have in recent years moved into a somewhat quieter, but no less disorienting, musical territory between stumbling exotica and out-of-tune fake folk, using synthesizers, home organs, theremin, and homemade instruments.
They're bringing with them their brand-new album ""Trikotin,"" consisting of eight tracks improvised and subsequently refined in a secret French studio, available in the most practical and versatile format imaginable: a 36-page, lovingly risographed sheet music book!

events.title: Practical Reflections on Intentional Kink Space Facilitation
events.description:
As Kink Space Facilitators, we experience a wide range of impressions in our work. We plan juicy offers, trauma and queer inclusive, and hold space for experiences, uncertainties, fuck ups, desires and much more. After planning and implementation comes reflection and evaluation. The ‘how was I’ as a professional and personally. 
Alexander Hahne, gay trans man, trainer and speaker for trans-specific topics in the field of sexual health, sex educator, somatic counselor, sexuality focussed bodyworker, systemic sex therapist, dancer and pleasure activist. Leader of workshops and individual counseling on the topics of body awareness, intimacy and sexuality. He works in the field of sexuality for about 20 years with almost 15 years of facilitation in pleasure and kink spaces. With his work he directly support them in their own experience of the body as well as the possibility of uncovering and using access to their own pleasurable potential. 
What happens in the workshop?
In this workshop, we will first put on our oxygen masks and subject our work to a reality check to see how it actually was. 
For example, we will address the following questions: 

Which methods worked really well and why?
Did the planning of your trauma-informed process have the desired effect during implementation?
Were there situations in which you felt uncertain or overwhelmed? What did you do then? What could be different next time?
Which methods did you use and why? What worked, what didn’t and why?

Yes, there is always too little time and the physical space is different than expected… how do you deal with that? How does that affect your stress level and facilitation? 
The approach is to separate your behaviour from you as a person. You as a person are highly valued and your behaviour is criticised. 
Note
This offering connects to and extends Ceci Ferox’s workshops Intentional Kink Space Facilitation and Intentional Kink Spaces: Structures and Organizing. You can purchase the recordings in our shop. If you did not have the opportunity to be part of these classes, we are offering the recordings for you to purchase as well. The recordings will be available until July 16th, 2026. This is optional, not mandatory. If you were part of one or both of these workshops, you can email us and get free access to the recordings again, if you purchase a ticket to this class.

There is something extraordinarily powerful in feeling and playing with consensual and voluntary pain. Why would a person want to feel pain? Why would another love to give it to someone else? How is pain and the processing of it changed depending on the context and relation it is put into? 
In the workshop, Mamana will go into a deep deep deep dive into all things pain and pain play. Together we will look at what pain actually is, how it is produced and interpreted in the brain and how it is influenced by personal, biological, social, and other contextual factors you can play with. We will go into the details of why people like to give and receive pain, how you can process it, which typical impact play instruments are helpful in inducing a certain kind of painful sensation. 
In short, this class will fry your brain with nerdy knowledge and allow you to think about your interest in pain play on a whole new level. Come for the facts, stay for the soul-searching of why sadomasochism is fucking delicious. 
What we will discuss

Define Pain?
Good pain, bad pain?
What do consent, trust and context have to do with it?

events.title: Peter Gall Quintet
events.description:
Winner GERMAN JAZZ AWARD “ALBUM OF THE YEAR” 2025
Winner BMW Welt Jazz Award 2021
Peter Gall is not only one of the most renowned and in-demand German drummers of his generation; he has also made a name for himself as an outstanding composer and a thoughtful bandleader, looking beyond the rim of the drum in a refined and deeply personal way. In 2018, he released his album Paradox Dreambox, a powerful musical statement that received euphoric international acclaim and led to successful tours and festival appearances.
Now Peter Gall presents his second brilliant album LOVE AVATAR, which won the German Jazz Prize 2025 in the category “Album of the Year.” His new songs tell striking stories, paint dreamlike collages, and—with great atmospheric density—search for fascinating musical galaxies, emotional eruptions, and the magic and love inherent in music.
Joining him is an absolute “dream band”: Wanja Slavin, Carl Morgan, Rainer Böhm, and Matthias Pichler are among the influential crème de la crème of the young, dynamic, and innovative European jazz scene. Perfectly attuned to one another, this tightly knit ensemble forms a powerful musical unit. Their performances are gripping, highly virtuosic, and deeply emotional at the same time, unleashing an onstage energy that is almost impossible to resist—unsurprisingly, the Peter Gall Quintet won the prestigious BMW Welt Jazz Award in 2021.

events.description:
Kick off your rope journey with a weekend that bundles our entire Rope Fundamentals series into one playful, beginner-friendly shibari workshop. 
Across two days, you’ll move from the simplest building blocks to a clear understanding of how harnesses work. Whether you’re brand new, brushing off old skills, or craving a solid base before exploring deeper techniques, this weekend is designed to set you up with confidence, creativity, and connection. 
You can bring someone to tie with or come solo and find a partner at the workshop. 
Join us for the full journey, or pick the day that suits you best: 
Get Your Saturday (Foundations & Fun), only ticket here.
Get your Sunday (Nerdery & Harnesses), only ticket here. 
Foundations & Fun
Saturday gives you the tools that make shibari fun — or intense, or meditative, or horny, or whatever flavor of rope you want to create. Ceci will get you started with the most essential techniques: the lark’s head, the single column tie, clean wrapping, managing tension, and staying safe. Once those basics are in place, we spend the rest of the day putting them to use in playful, intuitive ways.

Because rope isn’t static — people move — we’ll also practice guiding and responding to movement through levers, spirals, and simple transitions like sitting to standing or shifting limbs mid-tie.

Larkshead & single column tie
Rope safety

Playing with different intentions and moods
